questions.text: A single AA cannot deliver the Wi-Fi burst when it is half empty or cold (below about 10 C). How should we power the device?
options: Two AAA cells in series instead of one AA (recommended: half the current per cell, works down to 0 C until the cells are nearly empty, a bit more total energy, so about 1.5 years on alkaline, still to be confirmed; holder is wider but thinner)
One lithium AA only, never alkaline (about 2.5 USD per battery, about 2 years; an alkaline cell would stop Wi-Fi early)
One alkaline AA, and the device stops using Wi-Fi when the cell is half empty (about 5-10 months instead of 13)
One AA with a weaker Wi-Fi signal (shorter range in the house; still fails in a cold room)
questions.why: conflicts.md C17. The voltage converter can draw at most 0.65 A from the cell. With real efficiency (80-83 %) and a used or cold alkaline cell, a Wi-Fi connection needs more than that, so the device would reset during Wi-Fi. Two cells in series halve the current.

questions.text: The large energy-storage capacitor leaks a little current all the time, and the maker does not publish how much. What should we do?
options: Use a higher-voltage, low-leakage capacitor (recommended: about +0.4 USD, keeps battery life on target)
Keep the current part and measure 3 samples on the first boards
Accept a possible 4-5 % shorter battery life
questions.why: conflicts.md C15. 3 uA of leakage raises the average draw from 55 to 58 uA (13.4 months instead of 14 on one alkaline AA).

questions.text: Parts now cost about 27 USD per unit at 10 units, over your 25 USD wish. The two relays alone are about 18 USD because only one small relay fits the box. Is that acceptable for the prototypes?
options: Yes, accept about 27-28 USD for the 10 prototypes (recommended: look for cheaper relays only for production)
No, keep 25 USD: use a larger, cheaper relay and accept a tighter fit in the box
No, but I can pay a bit more for a relay with full safety insulation (about 11 USD each, removes the screw cover and breaker-off rule)
questions.why: conflicts.md C14 and C12. Cost is your top priority, but the relay price is set by the only part that fits the depth.
